summary: Standards: the third part of atip_checkl2input_20 (every write but init left out) asserts only assert_ne!(result, unsupported) for L2.input-normalise and L2.batch-ok, so it would pass for pass, fail or unprovided; the unprovided outcome is proved by the first part (member tag, batch rows) and by my probe (L2.input-normalise, -env, -pointer unprovided with 10 writes left out). L2.input-usage still asserts exit 2 itself (input.rs, usage check), unlike the other input rows after 1_3, which matches 'exit 2 is shorthand' only if L0.ok-exit also fails; a wrapper answering exit 1 there was not run.
